canonical_name: Post's problem on intermediate computably enumerable Turing degrees (source family; exact statement open)
literal_source_claim_zh: 是否存在严格介于可计算与完全之间的度
literal_source_claim_en: Whether there exists a degree strictly between the computable and complete degrees.
statement_blocker: The repository omits the computably enumerable restriction and Turing reducibility qualifier and gives no definitions, endpoint representatives, ordered binders, positive answer proposition, or source locator. Post's exact primary passage and the Friedberg-Muchnik solution statements, assumptions, direct-versus-incomparability relationship, proof boundaries, corrections, and independent review are not frozen. Selecting a c.e.-set encoding, bottom and complete degree, quotient representatives, or one solution formulation now would exceed intake evidence.
target_decision: retain the standard Post-problem family at provisional H1 and require immutable primary question and solution crosswalks plus independently reviewed encoding decisions before freezing a positive existence theorem
domain_and_universes: Expected universe 0 over subsets or predicates on natural numbers, or checked partial-function representatives of their Turing degrees. Exact c.e. model, quotient representation, endpoint construction, and set/oracle transport remain open.
conclusion: Expected source family: positive existence of a computably enumerable Turing degree strictly above the computable degree and strictly below the c.e.-complete halting degree. Exact source wording and Lean conclusion remain open.
